Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Park and Activities Commission Members will be
participating via teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city/agendas and available for
viewing thereafter.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
859 3881 1659, Meeting Password: 258521. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in
option from a phone line.)

-  Public  correspondence  may  be  emailed  to  Carol Corea, Administrative  Assistant  at
carolc@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded to
the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/agendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment”
button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After
you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting, may join by visiting http://www.zoom.com/join
and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 859 3881 1659, Meeting Password: 258521.

- If using a tablet or phone, download the Zoom app and enter the following credentials: Meeting ID: 859 3881
1659, Meeting Password: 258521.

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you
would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city/agendas.

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, JULY 6, 2020

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR CARMAN at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CARMAN led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioner’s Present:  Zigrang, Yoo, Schachter, Scott, Edler, Carman

  Commissioner’s Absent:  Medawar

  Staff Member’s Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, MAY 4, 2020

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF MAY 4, 2020.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the Planning
  Commission will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-19-19; LOCATION: 42 CLUB VIEW DRIVE, ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: MR. JONATHAN PARK; A request for approval of a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to construct one and two-story additions to a
  two-story residence. A Minor Deviation is required to decrease the front yard area by less
  than 10% and for the encroachment of the proposed addition into the required front yard
  which does not project closer to the property line than the forwardmost building line.

  Associate Planner Thom presented a summary of the staff report for Planning Application No. PA-
  19-19. At the Planning Commission meeting of February 3, 2020, this item was continued in order
  to address the Commission’s concerns. Per the guidance of the Planning Commission, the
  applicant eliminated the attached one story patio to help decrease the front width of the home; the
  front façade includes a roof eve to provide a visual break in the building mass; the area that was
  previously proposed as an ADU will remain as existing bonus room/library. The elimination of the
  ADU was not part of the Planning Commission’s guidance.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff is able to support the project and recommends that the
  Commission approve the project with the condition that the applicant work with staff to reduce the
  amount of metal standing seam roofing along the front elevation.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about a future proposal by the applicant for an ADU.
  Associate Planner Thom stated that if the proposed ADU is on the first floor, then it will be a
  ministerial review; however, if the proposed ADU is on the second floor, then it will need to come
  before the Planning Commission for review. Planning Manager Naughton added that if the

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING  1
MINUTES, JULY 6, 2020
   applicant proposed the ADU on the second floor in existing square footage, then it will also be a
  ministerial review, but a separate entrance would be required.

  CHAIR CARMAN asked if the staircase would require Planning Commission review. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that this is a gray area and would need input from the city attorney.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed concern with the standing seam roof separating the front
  door and window above it. Associate Planner Thom stated that it is a bit tricky in trying to find a
  natural break line in the roof and staff feels that there may need to be further refining of the eve.
  The intent it to break up the tower effect.

  Jonathan Park, Architect, stated that the property owners have agreed to use the same lightweight
  flat concrete tile material that is being used on the main house roof. Mr. Park stated that at the
  beginning of the project, the homeowners did not intend to propose an ADU. They thought that
  since it was now permitted, it would be a good use for the bonus room. They have now removed
  the proposal for the ADU and do not intend to add it in the future. The size has been reduced from
  5,863 sq. ft. to 5,076 sq. ft. to reduce the size and bulk of the home.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT inquired about the plans which show four vertical lines separating the
  four windows in the front living room. Mr. Park stated that this is part of the window and helps to
  break up the scale of the windows.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the exterior wall treatment. Mr. Park stated that in some
  places, it will be siding and stucco.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if support of this project has been received from the neighbor
  located to the east. Associate Planner Thom stated yes, an e-mail was received.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he saw a house similar to this in Redondo Beach, where
  a metal seam roof was used on the first floor and a shingle on the roof; the two mixed very well
  and broke up the monotony of the building.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-19-19 AND TO REDUCE THE STANDING
  SEAM TO AN ACCENT ITEM AS PRESENTED.

  Ayes: Carman, Edler, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang
  Noes:
  Absent: Medawar
  Abstain:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. PA-19-19, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to construct one and two-
  story additions to a two-story residence and two Minor Deviations. There is a 20-day appeal period,
  which will expire on July 27, 2020 where any member of the public may appeal the Planning
  Commission’s decision to the City Council.

  Chair Carman recused herself due to her proximity to the following subject property.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-191209; LOCATION: 2266 CARRIAGE DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: JOE SALZETTI; Per RHEMC Section
  17.72.110(C)(2), a six (6) month extension request for entitlements approved under
  Planning Commission Resolution No. PA-191209, including a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination (NC-190278); three Minor Deviations for reduction of the front yard area
  (MD-190280), additions in the front yard which do not project beyond the forwardmost
  building line (MD-190281), and a single story addition built along existing, nonconforming
  side yard setback building lines (MD-190-282); and a Variance for portions of the covered
  patio which would maintain less than the required rear yard setback (V-190279).

  Planning Manager Naughton presented Planning Application No. PA-191209, an extension request
  for entitlements approved under Planning Commission Resolution No. PA-191209. Following the
  February Planning Commission approval, the applicant was working with his architect to refine the
  architectural drawings just before the 20-day appeal expiration date of February 24, 2020, which
  was a few weeks prior to the Governor’s stay at home order. In addition, the applicant had health
  issues that took precedence over plan preparation.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
  a six month extension to entitlement approved under Resolution No. PA-191209, extending the life
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING  2
MINUTES, JULY 6, 2020
   of the approval to February 3, 2021.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that correspondence was submitted regarding this item and
  was included in the agenda packet as Attachment C. Ms. Naughton stated that the original
  entitlements were approved with the condition to require that, should the applicant not move
  forward with the project, the roof on the home would be required to be replaced. However, the
  Planning Commission has discretion on whether to approve the six month extension. The Planning
  Commission may wish to add a condition on the extension to replace the roof if the plans are not
  submitted to building and safety by the extension expiration date. The silhouette should have been
  removed, however this was also during the stay at home order. Code compliance will be working
  with the applicant to address other concerns mentioned in the correspondence.

  VICE CHAIR EDLER opened the public hearing

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR EDLER so ordered

  Joe Salzetti, Property Owner, stated that removing the two by fours used to attach the silhouette
  will destroy the roof and stated that he could cut remove the silhouette and leave the base.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG suggested to saw the silhouette and leave the base.

  VICE CHAIR EDLER closed the public hearing

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he is in favor with the suggestion to saw the silhouette and
  leave the base and has no issue with the extension.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the removal of the silhouette by July 30, 2020 could be
  made a condition.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-191209, AN EXTENSION FOR
  ENTITLEMENTS APPROVED UNDER PLANNING COMMISSION RESOLUTION
  NO. PA-191209 SUBJECT TO THE REMOVAL OF THE SILHOUETTE, BUT
  LEAVING THE BASE NEEDED FOR INTEGRITY OF THE ROOF.

  AYES: Edler, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang
  NOES:
  ABSENT: Medawar
  ABSTAIN: Carman

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved a six month
  extension for entitlements approved under Planning Commission Resolution No. PA-191209, this
  will extend the life of the approval to February 3, 2021. There is a 20-day appeal period, which will
  expire on July 27, 2020 where any member of the public may appeal the Planning Commission’s
  decision to the City Council. Staff will ensure that the silhouette is removed by the end of the month.

  Chair Carman rejoined the meeting

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked for status on the house on Lantana. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that the last information heard is that they are still within their timeframe for building permits
  and have six months to call for and inspection. Associate Planner Naughton stated that they are in
  plan check and were given a plan check extension. COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that the
  property is a hazard and the fencing is falling into a neighbor’s yard. Planning Manager Naughton
  stated that she will check-in with the City Attorney on requirements for fencing of the property due
  to security concerns, but the city is limited on what can be done since they have a valid plan check
  submittal.

  CHAIR CARMAN asked if there is an idea on a timeline for this project. Associate Planner Thom
  stated that the contractor was working on having a civil engineer sign off on plans since plans were
  revised so that a soils report is not required. Associate Planner Thom stated that she will follow-up
  with the building department on what they still need to submit. COMMISSIONER SCOTT requested
  that staff also contact the architect and the property owner.

  10.  PLANNING MANAGER ITEMS

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the city just signed a task order with Michael Baker

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING  3
MINUTES, JULY 6, 2020
   International to prepare a focused plan for the commercial district as part of the General Plan Update
  as part of the SB2 grant funds secured in April. As part of this fund, an ADU program will be
  developed. Drafts of the ADU plan will be presented to the Planning Commission.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that another grant that was applied for, if awarded, would be
  used to prepare for SB743, which would facilitate CEQA review when analyzing both development
  projects and public works projects.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that work on the Sustainability Element will begin when staff
  hears back from SCAG.

  CHAIR CARMAN stated that she is a member of the General Plan Advisory Committee and
  encouraged the Commissioner’s to review meeting minutes and get involved.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MAY 12, 2020

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MAY 26, 2020

  C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, JUNE 9, 2020 (BUDGET WORKSHOP)

  D.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, JUNE 9, 2020

  E.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, JUNE 23, 2020

  F.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, MAY 18, 2020

  G.  PARK AND ACITIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES, JUNE 15, 2020

  H.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES, JUNE 22, 2020

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A THROUGH 11H

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CARMAN adjourned the meeting at 7:46 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Bridget Carman, Chair
